subject.title: feat(gateway): add global auth rate limit mode for IP-agnostic brute-force protection

question: Should OpenClaw accept a permanent default-off `gateway.auth.rateLimit.global` mode in core after the loopback-reset, docs, and proof gaps are fixed?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically small, but it changes the Gateway auth brute-force boundary and introduces an intentional all-client lockout mode under attack.

options.title: Accept after security fixes
options.body: Sponsor the opt-in core config only after loopback resets cannot clear global remote lockouts, docs name the tradeoff, and real Gateway proof is posted.

options.title: Keep policy in the canonical issue
options.body: Pause this PR and keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101255 open until maintainers decide the broader public-exposure hardening policy.

options.title: Reject core config surface
options.body: Close the PR direction and document external identity-aware proxy or operational rate-limit approaches instead of adding another Gateway auth knob.

recommendation.title: Accept after security fixes
recommendation.body: Sponsor the opt-in core config only after loopback resets cannot clear global remote lockouts, docs name the tradeoff, and real Gateway proof is posted.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal for Gateway auth security policy among the likely owners and merged the original limiter work.
